story.summary: Four document pipelines become one shared loop. This page explains the change first, then shows how far you can trust each promise of the PR.
story.problem: Before this PR, each of the four documents (the clinician note, the UAP, the FMM and the 4H) had its own pipeline. Each pipeline loaded the CR, checked the draft, repaired it and called the Judges in its own way.
story.change: One harness now runs the same loop for all four documents. The loop makes a draft, checks it, repairs it, keeps or undoes each edit, and then releases or blocks the document.
story.trust: The main risk is an editor that hides a problem from the Judge and does not repair it. Type checks, import rules and anti-gaming rules stop this, and planted bugs prove most of these checks. The promises below show which parts are still weak.

loop.intro: One run makes one document from one finished CR. Each step below says what the loop does, and it links to the promise that protects that step.

steps.text: The harness loads the finished CR, and it refuses a CR that fails the CR-33 checks.
The generator of the document kind writes the first draft, and each kind uses only its own code.
The code checks, and the Judges of the chosen reflection mode, read the draft and report findings.
A gate sends the editor only the findings that a change to the files can repair.
The editor repairs the writable files, but it cannot delete a file or finish while a code check still blocks.
The note keeps each edit, but another kind keeps an edit only when the checks give a better score and no new severe finding.
The rounds stop when no fixable finding is left, when a round changes nothing, or at the round limit.
If the last draft of the note still blocks, the loop goes back to the last draft with no blocking finding.
For the note in the cr mode, a release audit runs the failed major checks again on the final draft.
The floor releases the document only when no guardrail finding is left, and else it blocks the document or uses a checked fallback.
The harness writes the document and a trace, and it sends the same model requests as the old code.

nodes.label: No: only the Judge grades it

steps.caption: A check or a Judge reports a finding. A gate decides if the editor can see it.
The editor does not see a finding that it must not change, or a result outside its own card. It also does not see a major finding that a second check did not repeat. Only the Judge grades these.
Only a finding that a change to the files can repair goes to the editor.
The editor changes only the writable files. It cannot delete a file, and it cannot finish while a code check blocks, up to three times.
The checks run again on the new draft and give a score.
The note keeps each edit. The other kinds keep an edit only when the score gets better and the edit adds no new severe finding.
For the other kinds, each other edit is undone and the files go back. A round that changed no file ends the rounds.

control_walkthroughs.title: Plant a bug, watch the check
control_walkthroughs.description: Each control plants one bug in a scratch copy and runs one check. K01b widens what the editor accepts. The type pin stayed green and missed it, but the project-wide type check (K35) went red on the same bug.

risks.why: Two greps show that `cr_service` does not import the harness today. No CI rule stops a new import after the merge.
risks.fix: Add a `cr_service` rule to `scripts/check_docgen_boundary.py` that refuses an import of `cr.docgen`. Then plant the import as a control.

risks.why: V36 skips when judiciary is not built, and it skips in CI. The control K36 stayed green, so the test cannot fail now.
risks.fix: Build judiciary in the CI test job, or make V36 fail, not skip, when the build is missing.

risks.why: Pin V01 stayed green on K01b, which widened the editor contract. Only the project-wide check V35 went red.
risks.fix: Add a pin that calls each editor with a plain `Finding` list, so that the pin file goes red on K01b.

risks.why: A packet and a ledger of different members could reach one document. No test gives `require_same_scope` a mismatched pair.
risks.fix: Add a test that gives `require_same_scope` a packet and a ledger of different members, and expects a refusal.

risks.why: A caller of the deleted `sheet_names` fails at run time. The PR assumes that no caller exists.
risks.fix: Record the project-wide type check, or a repo search for `sheet_names`, as a verifier for this claim.

risks.why: In diagnose mode, an unexpected tool call could give an empty error body. No test sends one.
risks.fix: Add a test that sends unexpected tool calls in diagnose mode, and checks that `submission_text` names them.

risks.why: Only the PR text says that the label is wrong. Nobody checked the plan.
risks.fix: Ask a clinician to read the UAP plan that the trace marks `released`.

risks.why: Nobody measured the default model change (#438) or the prompt-cache transport (#424) in production.
risks.fix: Measure both defaults in production before the merge, or ask the CR owner to decide, as the PR says.

risks.why: One Opus audit found no gaming. Opus is the author's model family, so the audit is one opinion counted twice.
risks.fix: Run the gaming audit again with a model from another family, in a fresh context.

risks.why: The note eval tested the #295 agent, not the note code in this PR.
risks.fix: Run the pre-registered note eval again on the code at the PR head.

tradeoffs: The run uses the PR's own tests as verifiers. It adds no new test to the PR.
Each control runs only the one test or check that backs its claim. A full CI run can see more, but it costs more time.
The run records the evals and does not run them again, so their verdict stays Backed.
concerns: V36 skips without a judiciary build, here and in CI. So C38 has no live verifier.
The type pin on line 36 (V01) checks that a Finding is not an EditableFinding. It does not check the parameter type of `Editor.edit`. V35 covers that edit.
C31 has only two greps (V37, V38). A boundary rule in CI that refuses an import of `cr.docgen` in `cr_service` would make it Proven.
C35, C36 and C37 are changes that the PR text does not name, and no test names their module.
V30, V31 and V32 use Opus, the same model family as the author.
The unclaimed list shows large new files, such as the UAP adapter and the command, that no claim cites.
verifications: Each verdict comes from scripts/verdicts.py, and the e2e test on the fixture checks that script.
Each control ran in a new scratch worktree of a local clone. The run deleted each worktree after the control.
Each red control matched its expected pattern, except K01b. K01b stayed green, and the map flags it.
No model call and no paid step ran. The env file set a dummy key and an unreachable base URL.
The mechanical checks (V37 to V39) read Git objects only. explain.py runs them again and stops when a result changes.
bullets: **Control missed:** pin L36 stayed green when K01b widened Editor.edit, EditorSpec.edit and NoteAuthorEditor.edit. Project-wide basedpyright (V35) went red on the same edit.
**Not run:** the evals and the Opus audit are recorded, not run again. Three of them use the author's model family.
